facility_roles.quote: operated at the Chooz nuclear power plant in France

intervals.label: concept proposed (nu-cleus)
intervals.note: The original 2017 concept paper investigates several possible reactor sites and a radioactive-source option; it does not name Chooz specifically. The Chooz site is confirmed only from 2022 onward (see next interval).
intervals.quote: a small-scale experiment, called nu-cleus, for the first detection of coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering

intervals.label: under construction at Chooz
intervals.quote: NUCLEUS is an experiment under construction based on ultra-low threshold (20 eVnr) cryogenic calorimeters

intervals.label: commissioning (technical run)
intervals.note: Status taken from the primary source rather than a secondary description; commissioning is ongoing as of 2026-09-17, with a Physics Run projected for the future.
intervals.quote: incorporating a data-driven treatment of the low-energy excess (LEE) observed during commissioning

quantity.quote: For the Technical Run with a 7 g CaWO4 target, we find competitive sensitivity

name: NUCLEUS
notes: The experiment's original spelling was 'nu-cleus'; it is not listed as an alias because it differs from 'NUCLEUS' only in punctuation.
Distance from the Chooz reactor core is not recorded: no source consulted gives it precisely; the collaboration's own wording is only 'very near' the core, closer than Double Chooz's near detector.

No official NUCLEUS website was found; none is recorded.

physics_goals.quote: enables CEνNS studies at extremely low momentum transfer and provides enhanced sensitivity to new physics ... a determination of the weak mixing angle at the lowest momentum transfer probed to date with CEνNS and leading CEνNS-based constraints on the neutrino charge radius and new mediator models
physics_goals.value: Measure CEvNS at the lowest nuclear-recoil energies yet attempted, for a low-momentum-transfer determination of the weak mixing angle and sensitivity to new physics (neutrino charge radius, new mediators)

summary.plain: A very small, super-cold detector at a French nuclear power plant, sitting closer to the reactor core than any similar experiment, built to catch antineutrinos at the gentlest nudges ever attempted.
summary.technical: NUCLEUS: reactor CEvNS experiment using gram-scale CaWO4 (and originally Al2O3) cryogenic calorimeters with a ~20 eV(nr) nuclear-recoil threshold, sited very near the reactor core of the EDF Chooz B nuclear power plant, France. Proposed as the 'nu-cleus' concept in 2017, under construction by 2022, and in commissioning (Technical Run, 7 g CaWO4 target, with an observed low-energy excess under study) as of the most recent sourced publication (2026).
